conventions.sums: Sum all ten measured samples at each of the three source lengths; natural_greedy sums its ten measured samples separately.
conventions.nonoverlapping: first_token_latency + decode_including_greedy_readback + natural_greedy; do not add prefill or decode_model_only again because these are contained intervals.
conventions.decode_model_only: Each interval encloses model.decode plus the following Backend::sync; the preceding sync and subsequent argmax/readback are outside. This is not pure GPU kernel time.
conventions.unassigned: Warmup samples, reference validation, cache allocation outside timers, authentication, report/metadata work and process overhead are not assigned per-phase CPU counters.

controlled_pair.summary: Historical source rebuilt and current source match within the retained controlled median comparisons; this does not erase the original historical failure.

binary_path_observation.scope: Only this named path was rehashed at the observation time; no claim that a different copy of the original binary cannot exist. Its current contents must not be used as an exact replay of the original dd8a19df executable.

limitations: Retired instructions, CPU cycles and CPU seconds are whole-process counters, not counters for the timed decode intervals. The phase sums localize wall time only.
Increased host work can reflect submission/dispatch, synchronization polling or waiting on slower GPU execution. It does not establish CPU causation or a specific Metal kernel regression.

The original and rebuilt records describe the same hardware, OS build, backend name and AC powermode=0. They do not capture continuous GPU clocks, thermal state, kernel selections, tuning-cache contents or exact competing desktop GPU load.
The newer environment explicitly lists ordinary desktop GPU consumers; the older description is less specific. That documentation difference is not proof that those processes were absent before.
No swapping is recorded, but this does not establish absence of memory pressure or bandwidth contention.

Rebuilt/current runtime-control endpoints match and are unchanged, but the original run has no equivalent captured runtime-control file. Same configuration discovery is not a frozen runtime/tuning cache.
All observations and binary hashes describe their recorded historical times, not an arbitrary future HEAD or filesystem state.

preserve: exact test filter and one test thread
identical checkpoint/reference hashes and greedy oracle
three warmups and ten measured repetitions at each existing shape
128 forced decode tokens, cache capacities and all existing synchronization/timer boundaries
minimal_follow_up_protocol.cpu_sampling: During a timestamped warm forced-decode interval, attach /usr/bin/sample PID 10 1 -mayDie -file NEW_OUTPUT_PATH; do not interpret its sampled stack counts as retired-instruction counters.
minimal_follow_up_protocol.telemetry: For the diagnostic run, collect continuous 1000 ms powermetrics tasks,cpu_power,gpu_power,thermal with per-process GPU and IPC observations, subject to sampling privileges. Record competing GPU use, frequencies and thermal pressure without changing power settings.
minimal_follow_up_protocol.phase_alignment: Add only opt-in nonblocking diagnostic timestamps outside the existing timers if exact alignment is needed; the current ordinary timing report lacks absolute phase timestamps. Do not substitute the memory-supervisor ACK protocol, which perturbs scheduling.
minimal_follow_up_protocol.full_gpu_trace_requirement: A per-kernel Metal timeline requires making full Xcode/xctrace available through a developer directory. Nothing was installed or selected during this audit.
minimal_follow_up_protocol.interpretation: CPU stacks plus GPU activity distinguish where present warm-loop time is spent; they cannot retrospectively identify the original run cause without comparable historical evidence. Retain profiled results separately from acceptance timings and keep the historical failure unresolved.
